title: Categories + cross-project filtering
description:
## Parent

sutra/150 — Code-anchored lessons: sutra_remember / contextual surfacing

## What to build

Category-based filtering so that lessons surface only in relevant workspaces. Categories are flat tags (multi-valued) on each lesson. When surfacing, sutra filters by the current workspace's language and technology stack — a Dart project never sees rust-only lessons, but does see sqlite-general ones.

Category dimensions:
- **Technology**: rust, dart, flutter, sqlite, rusqlite, diesel, etc.
- **Architectural**: mcp-server, cli, daemon, indexer, state-management
- **Concern**: concurrency, error-handling, sentinel-values, migration, testing

`sutra_remember` accepts optional explicit categories. Category inference from the workspace graph (file language, imports) comes in the enrichment slice (sutra/157).

Surfacing: `query_for_context()` accepts the workspace's language/tech profile and filters out lessons whose categories are all irrelevant to the workspace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Categories stored per-lesson in the `categories` table
- [ ] `sutra_remember` accepts optional `categories` parameter
- [ ] `query_for_context()` accepts workspace language/tech profile and filters by category relevance
- [ ] Lessons with no categories surface in all workspaces (uncategorized = universal)
- [ ] Lessons tagged only `[rust]` do not surface in a Dart workspace
- [ ] Lessons tagged `[sqlite]` (no language tag) surface in both Rust and Dart workspaces
- [ ] Tests: category filtering, universal lessons, cross-project scenarios
